extracted.intended_audience: educators, teachers, students of education, educational philosophers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying criteria for judging educational theories and for designing educational practice (curriculum, method, and subject-matter selection). Focuses on whether education fosters growth, social competence, appropriate methods, and meaningful subject-matter relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result: capacity for further education
rubrics_metrics.description: The conception that the result of the educative process is capacity for further education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should aim to develop the learner's ability to continue learning; this contrasts with theories which orient education chiefly toward some fixed future duty or toward merely reproducing past culture. Anti-pattern: treating education as a one-time preparation that exhausts its purpose once a specific skill or body of knowledge is 'completed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on immediate present needs and possibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of the needs and possibilities of the immediate present rather than diverting attention to remote future duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should be grounded in present situations and opportunities that the learner actually encounters; focusing on distant hypothetical duties defeats practical learning. Example: prefer tasks that address current social or practical problems instead of abstract future-oriented drills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid preparing chiefly for some future duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of preparing or getting ready for some future duty diverts attention from present needs and thereby defeats its own purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize hypothetical future roles over present development. Anti-pattern: curricula built only to 'prepare' students for unspecified future responsibilities at the cost of present meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject 'unfolding from within' when it ignores present interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion that education is merely an unfolding from within (as in some Froebel/Hegel variants) is defective when it neglects interaction between present organic tendencies and present environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational plans must account for how current instincts/tendencies interact with available environment and materials. Anti-pattern: assuming latent potential will simply emerge without providing appropriate present stimuli and social opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not subordinate individual development to institutional conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of Hegelian views: education should not be mere obedient assimilation to existing institutions or social organism roles that deny individual development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should promote individual growth and not merely train persons to occupy fixed class or institutional roles. Anti-pattern: justifying rigid class distinctions by analogies to bodily organs or social organism metaphors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter-centered formation (Herbartian steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is formation by means of subject matter presented from without; method includes steps of preparation (activate prior presentations), presentation, interaction of new and old content, and application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should select and sequence material so new presentations interact with and build upon prior ideas. Example sequence: preparation -> presentation -> interaction -> application. Use this as a deliberate method, but be aware of risks of over-formalization that ignore active native functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select proper material and sequence based on prior ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: The educator's business is (1) to select the proper material to fix original reactions and (2) to arrange the sequence of subsequent presentations on the basis of the store of ideas secured by prior transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum design must be sensitive to learners' existing ideas (apperceiving background) and plan sequences that facilitate assimilation and reinforcement. Anti-pattern: random sequencing or assuming one universal sequence fits all learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training of faculties must be tied to concrete subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory of 'formal discipline' (training general faculties by repetition) is fallacious when it treats subject matter as external and indifferent; there is no such thing as an ability to see/hear/remember in general—abilities are tied to specific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises intended to develop attention, memory, judgment, etc., must involve meaningful subject matter relevant to the purposes for which those abilities are needed. Anti-pattern: isolated drills (e.g., rote memorization of meaningless lists) that claim to build abstract faculties transferable to all domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training is selective coordination of responses, not mere repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective training consists in selecting from diffuse responses those adapted to the stimulus and coordinating stimuli and responses—rather than merely exercising a putative faculty by repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities that shape which responses are reinforced and how different responses coordinate (e.g., linking visual cues, manual actions, sounds, and verbal labels). Example: learning to grasp an object is not muscle strengthening alone but selection and coordination of sensory and motor patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization reduces transfer; social breadth yields general education
rubrics_metrics.description: The more specialized the adjustment of response and stimulus, the less generally available the training; conversely, activities broad in scope and socially embedded produce flexible, general education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor varied, socially-contextualized activities (games, social tasks) over uniform mechanical exercises if the goal is general adaptability. Anti-pattern: narrow drill leading to skill narrowly limited to one act (e.g., practicing letter forms without context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of subject-matter selection must be social usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: We should determine what sort of subject matter we wish the pupil to become expert in and for what purpose; the criterion must be social—what makes the learner an effective member of the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select content and modes of engagement according to social roles, community needs, and meaningful purposes. Example: observe and recall those things that matter for participation in the learner's social group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid isolating subject matter from social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation of subject matter from social context obstructs securing a general training of mind; literature, art, religion dissociated from social relations are as narrowing as technical training alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate humanistic and technical subject matter into social contexts and practical activities to broaden coordination of responses. Anti-pattern: teaching literature or art only as ornament divorced from present social meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use past cultural products as present resources, not retrospective standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of past products should serve present needs and problems; making records of the past the main material of education risks making the past a rival of the present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ historical/cultural materials to illuminate and resolve contemporary problems; do not treat them as templates that students must recapitulate. Anti-pattern: insisting students reenact past cultural stages (recapitulation theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize heredity as a limit but focus on environmental utilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Heredity signifies the original endowment (native activities) and is a limit of education; but education's task is to study aptitudes and furnish environments that function for whatever activities are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess native aptitudes as a practical preliminary, but design environments and opportunities to activate and coordinate those aptitudes. Example: if vocal apparatus exists, ensure social verbal environment to develop language; do not attempt impossible training when native equipment is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation is reconstruction/reorganization via native activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Education forms character and mind by selection and coordination of native activities so they may utilize subject matter; formation is a process of reconstruction and reorganization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim at reorganizing and coordinating learners' active tendencies with meaningful subject matter rather than imposing static content. Anti-pattern: pedagogies that treat learners as passive receptacles of content without opportunities to reorganize their activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware over-formalized universal method
rubrics_metrics.description: Herbart's claim of a perfectly uniform method for all subjects and pupils (preparation, presentation, interaction, application) risks exaggerating the power of consciously formulated procedures and underestimating unconscious/vital attitudes and active functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use methodical steps as useful tools but adapt them to the individuality and active functions of learners; do not enforce a mechanical one-size-fits-all pedagogy.
